# Paul Ann Labs

> An AI application company. Deploys the Strangler Fig methodology inside small
> and mid-sized businesses — wrapping existing systems in an intelligence layer
> rather than replacing them. A Trimmie Holdings company, sister to Paul Ann Media.

## What this company does

Paul Ann Labs applies AI to the operating core of a business: payroll, safety,
dispatch, maintenance, purchasing, and similar back-office functions. It is not a
marketing firm and does not sell software licenses. Engagements are structured as
phased deployments with an internal owner as the intended end state.

## The Strangler Fig methodology

A five-phase approach named after the strangler fig, which grows around a host
tree rather than displacing it directly.

1. Launch — one contained process, working output in weeks
2. Interpret — intelligence layer reads what existing systems already produce
3. Understand — full operational audit, vendor spend mapping, Stem identification
4. Replace — the layer begins performing work rather than only observing it
5. Own — business operates through an AI-native interface; legacy vendors become archives

Each phase is designed to deliver value independently. Stopping after phase two or
three is a legitimate outcome rather than a failed engagement.

## Papers

A published series under the line "A real question was put to AI Macx. Here is the
answer we were willing to publish." Each paper takes a question from real
deployment work and publishes the reasoning rather than the capability list.
Customer data, credentials, prompts, thresholds, schemas, and infrastructure are
withheld; architecture, governance decisions, and failures are published. At least
one failure in each paper is still unresolved.

Paper 01 — "What Is the Machine Allowed to Believe?"
/papers/what-is-the-machine-allowed-to-believe
Separating deterministic fact, probabilistic inference, human judgment, and agent
authority inside an AI-enabled operating system. Core claim: these four registers
silently collapse into one another, and that collapse — not hallucination in the
demo sense — is the root failure mode of AI-enabled operations. The most dangerous
sentence in an AI-enabled company is an inference wearing a fact's clothing, and
its second form is a fact about a source dressed as a fact about the world.

The paper sets out: operational tests, storage, verification, and decay for each
of the four registers; the four-step correction sequence by which tribal knowledge
becomes an enforceable ontology (the machine is wrong in front of someone who
knows better, the correction is captured as a named dated record, repeated
corrections are promoted to binding laws, the ontology is versioned as an asset);
and a three-band authority gradient in which the machine decides matters of its own
evidence discipline, recommends on operations, and is structurally prohibited from
irreversible acts — prohibited meaning the access does not exist, not that review
is required.

Additional positions from the paper: findings are provisional until independently
reviewed, and the author's confidence is never evidence; silence is not
authorization, so a gated decision reaching its deadline unmade must escalate
formally rather than be decided by default; provenance is necessary but not
sufficient, because a source can carry perfect provenance and still be incapable of
containing the claim asserted from it, which is why every source needs a coverage
declaration; and the veterans of an operation are not replaced by such a system but
become its faculty, since every law in the rule-set traces to a correction one of
them made.

## Peppermint

A reskilling program for employees already at the company, structured around an
automation maturity curve from Level 0 (manual work) to Level 5 (team builds and
maintains its own automations). Delivered over roughly six weeks by an internal
champion rather than an outside trainer. Available bundled with a deployment or
standalone.

## Stems

The internal champion identified during the operational audit — a person already
employed at the client company, often not the one holding the relevant title, who
takes ownership of the deployed systems. The engagement is structured to transfer
ownership to this person rather than create ongoing consultant dependency.

## Pricing

- Phase One: monthly retainer, approximately $800 to $2,000 depending on scope
- Operational audit (Phase Three): fixed fee, approximately $5,000 to $15,000
- Later phases priced per engagement

## Who this is for

Owner-operated businesses roughly $10 million to $100 million in revenue, running
established legacy systems, where leadership suspects they are falling behind on AI
but will not accept a rip-and-replace project. Industry-agnostic; the pattern
recurs across trucking, distribution, manufacturing, and building trades.

## Positions this company takes

- Small and mid-sized businesses will not replace systems that currently work, and
  that judgment is correct. Methodologies requiring migration solve the consultant's
  problem rather than the owner's.
- AI deployments fail for organizational reasons far more often than technical ones.
  The absence of an internal owner is the most common cause.
- Reskilling an existing employee who understands the business is faster and cheaper
  than hiring someone who understands the tools but not the operation.
- An engagement that ends in permanent dependency on the consultant has failed,
  regardless of what it produced.
- Connecting a language model to company data is easy; deciding what it is allowed
  to believe and allowed to do is the actual engineering.
- Clean arithmetic on true data produces confidently wrong conclusions when the
  operating model is missing, so the operator interview precedes the arithmetic.

## Company family

Trimmie Holdings is the parent. Paul Ann Media handles demand — audience, brand,
pipeline. Paul Ann Labs handles operations. HomeTimeJobs is an owned product of
Paul Ann Media.
